title: Canada's national emergency alert system will sound off Wednesday for testing
summary: Canada's National Public Alerting System is running tests of its Alert Ready system Wednesday across all provinces and territories. Alert Ready delivers alerts about critical events such as…

image.caption: A test of Canada's emergency alert system is set for Wednesday, Nov. 18. (Sean Kilpatrick/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Canada's National Public Alerting System is running tests of its Alert Ready system Wednesday across all provinces and territories. Alert Ready delivers alerts about critical events such as tornadoes, flooding, fires and Amber alerts.
Alert Ready test will be broadcast on TV, radio and delivered to wireless devices
There's (probably) no need to take cover if your phone, radio or television blasts out the telltale sounds of an emergency alert Wednesday.

Canada's National Public Alerting System is running tests of its Alert Ready system across all provinces and territories. Alert Ready delivers alerts about critical events such as tornadoes, flooding, fires and Amber alerts.
The test will be broadcast on television and radio and delivered to compatible wireless devices connected to an LTE or 5G network.

blocks.text: "This public test helps ensure the system continues to function effectively and helps Canadians recognize alert signals in the event of a real emergency," Pelmorex, which operates the technical infrastructure of Alert Ready, said in a news release.
The test will simulate an emergency alert, beginning with its distinctive tone, followed by a message that will "clearly indicate that it is a test and that no action is required."
Here's when the tests will happen in each province and territory at local times:
Canadians cannot opt out, Pelmorex noted, "because the system is designed to warn Canadians of imminent threats to life and property."
Tests typically take place in May and November. The CRTC requires wireless service providers and broadcasters to issue at least one public test alert per year, Pelmorex said.
So far in 2026, the system has delivered more than 1,215 emergency alert messages across Canada, notes the news release.
